rationale: This 50/50 partnership structure has significant risks. The equal split creates deadlock potential on all major decisions. The shotgun clause and drag-along rights allow hostile actions by either partner. The 24-month non-compete in the entire data analytics industry is overly broad. The $120K salary is below market for SF. The buyout valuation method may undervalue the business. Death forces estate to sell. However, the partnership allows shared risk and complementary skills (CEO + CTO).
required_changes: Consider 51/49 split or rotating tiebreaker to prevent deadlock
Remove or significantly limit shotgun clause (require cause, not at-will)
Reduce non-compete to 12 months and narrow to direct competitors only
Increase salaries to market rate ($150K-170K) or at least $140K
Improve buyout valuation: use DCF or include IP value
Allow death/disability to result in passive ownership for estate/disabled partner
Limit drag-along to qualified sales above certain valuation threshold
Add independent board seat or advisor for tiebreaking
Cap additional capital requirements or set clear funding milestones
Add good leaver/bad leaver provisions for fault-based separations
Extend shotgun response time from 30 to 60-90 days
Add vesting schedule for equity (4-year vest) to prevent early departure
deal_breakers: If shotgun clause cannot be removed or limited
If non-compete cannot be reduced below 18 months
If salary cannot be increased to reasonable market rate
If no tiebreaker mechanism can be added for 50/50 deadlock
when_acceptable: This structure works if: (1) partners have deep trust and aligned vision, (2) both have adequate liquidity for shotgun scenario, (3) willing to accept below-market salary initially, (4) committed for long term (5+ years), (5) have strong communication and conflict resolution skills
